messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: linker error
parts:
Sometime recently, I've become unable to link the "Getting Started" example:

goodrich@CYBERPOWERPC:/opt/stan$ make clean-all
goodrich@CYBERPOWERPC:/opt/stan$ make CC=clang++ O=3 bin/libstan.a bin/stanc
goodrich@CYBERPOWERPC:/opt/stan$ bin/stanc src/models/basic_distributions/normal.stan
goodrich@CYBERPOWERPC:/opt/stan$ clang++ -v -O0 -Lbin -lstan -Isrc -Ilib/boost_1.50.0 -Ilib/eigen_3.1.1 anon_model.cpp

Linker error log attached. Anybody have a guess as to what is going on? It is the same with g++.

Ben

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] linker error
parts:
On 8/23/12 7:22 PM, Ben Goodrich wrote:
> Sometime recently, I've become unable to link the "Getting Started" example:

The two variables that your linker is choking on are
global variables defined in agrad.hpp.

anon_model.cpp:(.text+0x4798): undefined reference to `stan::agrad::var_stack_'
anon_model.cpp:(.text+0x47b5): undefined reference to `stan::agrad::memalloc_'

It's the only place we use global variables.

The declarations in agrad.hpp are now marked as "extern",
with the unmarked declarations in agrad.cpp. In fact,
that's all that's in agrad.cpp other than an include of
agrad.hpp.

I'm not sure why you're having an issue linking it.
It's fine on the Mac and Windows.

If I try to declare (rather than extern) the variables in
agrad.hpp and leave agrad.cpp as a shell that only has
the include, the linker bombs with multiple definitions
across translation units. Which is confusing to me because
there are other class definitions in agrad.hpp (though not
any bare function definitions).

- Bob

P.S. With the latest patch to stanc, the model name will
be based on the class name. I'm about to modify the doc.

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] linker error
parts:
Yup -- works just fine that way.

I think this is around the fifth time we've
revisited this "where does -lstan" go.
Sorry to muddy the waters yet again with
the manual. I'll change it right now.

In fact, I'm going to move the getting started
instructions to a (very simply formatted and
hence easy to reformat) web page and suggest that people
look at the output of make to see what actual
commands are being given to C++.

The doc started when we were in the simpler
header-only lib, then we broke out Boost and Eigen,
and given that I don't know where this will stop,
I think it's best to lean back on make.

No wonder all these C++ projects are so
damn complex.

- Bob
